title: Robot not connecting on the field
summary: Driver station to FMS, radio link, roboRIO link. Work left to right on the field monitor.

start.question: Look at the field monitor, left to right. What is the first thing that is not green?
start.help: The DS reports every status. The radio cannot show linked until the DS is linked, and the RIO cannot show linked until the radio is.

options.label: All green but the robot drops or lags in matches

ds-ethernet.question: On the DS laptop, open the Diagnostics tab. Is Enet Link lit?
ds-ethernet.help: Enet Link means the laptop sees something on its Ethernet port. If it is off, nothing else matters yet.

options.label: Yes, but FMS is still red

ds-no-ethernet.title: DS laptop has no Ethernet link
steps: Unplug the field cable from the laptop and plug it back in until it clicks. Check the other end at the player station.
If the laptop uses a USB Ethernet adapter, unplug the adapter and plug it back in. Try a different USB port.
Run ncpa.cpl. Make sure the Ethernet adapter is enabled and not disabled or greyed out.
Try the spare field cable or a different player station port. Ask the FTA for one.
If the port still shows no link, use a USB Ethernet adapter from the team or a loaner laptop. Tell the FTA.

ds-team-number.question: Open the DS Setup tab. Does the team number match the team in this match?

ds-wrong-team.title: Fix the team number in the DS
steps: Type the correct team number in the Setup tab and press Enter. Click outside the box so it takes effect.
Wait about 10 seconds. The FMS light on the field monitor should turn green.
If a shared laptop is used by two teams, check it every match.

ds-no-fms.title: DS has link but no FMS
steps: Make sure the FRC Driver Station software is open and is not a second copy. Close and reopen it.
Turn the Wi-Fi off with the hardware switch or Quick Settings. Disable every other network adapter in ncpa.cpl so only the field Ethernet is left.
Set the Ethernet adapter to Automatic (DHCP). On the field, FMS hands out 10.TE.AM.x addresses.
Turn off all three Windows Defender Firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public). Remove third-party antivirus firewalls.
In an admin command prompt run ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew.
Still red: swap to the spare field cable, then to a loaner laptop. Escalate to the FTA.

radio-lights.question: Look at the radio on the robot. What do the lights show?
radio-lights.help: VH-109 lights, left to right: PWR, SYS, 2.4G, 6G, RIO.

options.label: PWR on, SYS blinking about once a second

radio-no-power.title: Radio has no power
steps: Confirm the robot is on and the main breaker is in. Check the roboRIO Power light is green.
Tug the radio power connector. Reseat the Weidmuller plug or the PoE cable in the RIO port.
Find the PDH or PDP channel that feeds the radio. Check the fuse or breaker is seated and the channel LED is not red.
If PoE and the DC input are both wired, unplug one. Use one source only.
If the radio stays dark with known good power, swap in a spare radio. Tell the FTA so it can be programmed for this event.

radio-not-linked.title: Radio is up but cannot reach the field
steps: Wait 60 seconds after power on. The radio takes that long to boot and join the field.
Ask if the radio was programmed at this event's kiosk. A radio from a previous event or home has the wrong key. Reprogram it at the kiosk.
Make sure only one radio on the robot is powered. A spare radio left on confuses the field.
Check the DS is fully connected first. The radio cannot link until the DS is.
Still blinking after a reprogram: swap the radio and escalate to the FTA to check the field AP.

radio-ap-mode.title: Radio is in access point mode on battery
steps: All lights blinking fast means the radio is set to Access Point mode and sees battery power. Wireless is off in this state.
Take the radio to the kiosk and reprogram it in Robot Radio mode for this event.
If the team has two radios, check the other one is not the AP unit by mistake.
If the lights stay this way after a reprogram, swap the radio and tell the FTA.

radio-linked-monitor-red.title: Radio pings the field but the monitor shows it red
steps: SYS solid means the radio can ping the field. The monitor turns green only after the DS is fully connected.
Go back to the DS. Confirm Enet Link, team number, and FMS green.
Wait 20 seconds after the DS turns green. The radio column follows.
If the DS is green and the radio stays red, swap the radio and escalate to the FTA.

rio-lights.question: Look at the roboRIO. What are the Power and Status lights doing?

rio-no-link.title: roboRIO booted but has no link to the radio
steps: Check the Ethernet cable from the RIO goes into the radio port labeled RIO, not AUX or DS.
Look for link lights at both Ethernet ends. Reseat both plugs. A cable with a broken latch clip must be replaced.
Swap the Ethernet cable for a known good one.
If the RIO Ethernet port shows no link with a good cable, plug a USB Ethernet adapter into the RIO USB port and connect the radio to it. This has got robots on the field with a dead port.
Press the reset button on the RIO. If nothing changes, swap the roboRIO and call the CSA.

rio-status-blink.title: roboRIO Status light is blinking
steps: A blinking Status light after boot means the RIO is not running normally. Count the blinks.
roboRIO 2: pull the microSD card, check the slot for debris, reseat it fully. Reboot.
Groups of 2 or 3 blinks: reboot. If it repeats, reimage the RIO.
Constant flashing (RIO 2) or 4 flashes then a pause (RIO 1): unrecoverable. Reimage the card or the RIO. If that fails, swap the roboRIO.
Use the roboRIO guide in this app for the full breakdown. Call the CSA if the team has no spare.

rio-power.title: roboRIO power problem
steps: Off: check the RIO power Weidmuller plug and the PDH or PDP RIO channel fuse. Tug test the wires.
Amber: brownout. Check battery voltage in the DS. Swap to a fully charged battery.
Red: short on a user rail. Unplug everything from the RIO power rails and DIO, then power cycle.
Check the main breaker lug nuts and battery connector are tight. Loose main power causes both amber and off.
If the light stays red with nothing plugged in, swap the roboRIO and call the CSA.

no-code.title: Everything green but No Code
steps: In the DS, click Restart Robot Code. Wait 15 seconds.
Ask if the code changed since it last worked. Check the DS Console for a stack trace or a crash message.
Reboot the roboRIO from the DS or with the reset button. Wait for the Status light to turn off.
If the code was deployed with a different WPILib year than the RIO image, it will not run. Redeploy.
Use the Code and deploy guide in this app. Hand off to the CSA if it still shows No Code.

drops.title: Robot connects but drops or lags during matches
steps: Check where the radio is mounted. It should be near the top of the robot, in the open, away from motors and not inside a metal box or a 3D printed enclosure.
Tug the radio power and Ethernet plugs. A loose Weidmuller or a cable without a latch drops the link under vibration. Tie-wrap the power cable.
If the radio is powered by both PoE and the DC input, remove one. Dual power from two sources causes reboots.
Check the DS log for battery voltage dips under 7 V. A brownout resets the radio if it is on a poor supply. Lower motor current limits.
Check the DS for high trip time or packet loss and let the FTA know so they can watch the AP side.
